scope: Actual RabbitMQ broker, Pika client, and SQLite transactions. Research probe, not a reusable implementation.

setup.ledger: SQLite WAL with synchronous=FULL; logical-operation claim and effect in one transaction
setup.identity: Application operation ID; broker delivery tag and redelivered flag are not identity

method.commit_before_ack: Publish confirmed persistent message; manually receive; atomically commit operation claim and effect; close the AMQP connection without ACK; reconnect; observe redelivered=true; repeated claim inserts no row; effect remains one; ACK and confirm empty queue.
method.independent_duplicate: Republish identical operation ID; observe redelivered=false because this is a new publication; persisted claim still suppresses the second effect.
method.rollback: Apply claim and effect then roll back; close connection unacknowledged; redelivery commits exactly one effect.
method.unsafe_control: ACK followed by synchronous queue-declare round trip, then disconnect before the DB effect; reconnect sees an empty queue and effect count zero.

applicability.trigger: A broker message mutates local transactional state and may be redelivered after a connection or consumer failure.
applicability.failure: Acknowledgement before commit can lose work; commit before acknowledgement can produce duplicate attempts.
applicability.mechanism: Commit the stable operation claim and local effect atomically, then acknowledge; on redelivery reuse that identity and return the existing outcome.
conditions: Claim and business effect share one transactional database boundary.
Ledger identity is stable across republishing as well as broker redelivery.
Retention covers the legitimate redelivery and replay horizon.
applicability.counterexample: A payment provider call and local ledger do not share this SQLite transaction; this probe does not establish atomicity for external effects.
applicability.verification: Four observed broker/DB cases, including unsafe-order negative control. Add external-outcome reconciliation and crash/failover tests when those guarantees are required.

limits: One local broker and local SQLite file, no HA/quorum or disk/power-loss experiment.
Broker process was not restarted; durable flags are configuration, not an observed restart proof.
External side effects, inbox expiration, schema evolution, parallel consumers, DLX/quarantine persistence, and failover were not tested.
Connection close was graceful AMQP shutdown, not a killed process or network partition.
SQLite connections were reopened to inspect persisted state; the laptop and broker process were not crashed.
No latency, throughput, partition ownership, ordering, or bounded-prefetch guarantee was measured.

artifacts.persistence_note: Raw probe artifacts are local temporary research files; the repository evidence records observations but does not promise those paths survive cleanup.

sources.purpose: Publisher confirmations and consumer acknowledgements cover separate boundaries.
Quorum and dead-letter safety requirements were researched separately; this classic-queue experiment does not validate them.
